GENERAL HEADQUARTERS
SUPREME COMMANDER FOR THE ALLIED POWERS
AG 019 (20 Nov 46) ESS/FI
(SCAPIN-1348)
APO 500
20 November 1946
MEMORANDUM FOR : IMPERIAL JAPANESE GOVERNMENT.
THROUGH : Central Liaison Office, Tokyo.
Subject : Dissolution of the Central life Insurance Corporation and of the Central Non-Life Insurance Corporation.
1. In order to stimulate revival of private insurance business in all types of insurance contracts and to provide equal opportunity to firms and individuals to compete in the insurance business, the Imperial Japanese Governmenf is hereby directed to take the necessary action to:
a. Dissolve the Central Life Insurance Corporation and the Central Non-Life Insurance Corporation, and repeal or rescind all laws and regulations giving them legal existence, and preserve the complete records of these corporations within the Ministry of Finance.
b. Liquidate the assets of the Central Life Insurance Corporation and the Central Non-Life Insurance Corporation under the supervision of the Liquidation Branch, Finance Division, Economic and Scientific Section, in accordance with the Commercial Code and existing price control and currency regulations and policies of the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers.
2. The Imperial Japanese Government is directed to submit a plan for the dissolution of these corporations as outlined in subparagraph 1b above, within thirty (30) days of the date of this memorandum. This plan will include such steps as are necessary to assure maximum protection to the interests of the allied-owned insurance companies.
3. Direct communication between agencies of the Imperial Japanese Government and interested Staff Sections of General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, is authorized to implement this memorandum.
FOR THE SUPREME COMMANDER:
JOHN B. COOLEY,
Colonel, AGD,
Adjutant General.

MEMO FOR RECORD: (SCAPIN - 1348)
WKL/DAM/ng
18 October 1946
1. A staff study on the dissolution of the Central Life Insurance Corporation and the Central Non-Life Insurance Corporation is attached.
2. It is recommended that this memorandum be issued to the Japanese Government directing the dissolution of the above named Japanese Government Corporations.
3. The interests of USAFIK have been considered. This action does not affect the Korean area.
4. This is considered an administrative matter. No surveillance by the EIGHTH Army is required.
5. Concurrences: ESS/LE; ESS/AC; GS; CPC.
W. K. L.
